This criminal appeal under Section 14A(1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (hereinafter to be referred as 'the SC/ST Act')
has been filed on behalf of the appellant being aggrieved with the order dated 16.08.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge, SC/ST (POA) Act Cases, Sriganganagar (hereinafter to be referred as 'trial court') in Criminal Misc. Case No.301/2023, whereby the trial court has dismissed the bail application filed on behalf of the appellant.

sentences.text: The appellant has been arrested in FIR No.275/2021 registered at Police Station Anoopgarh, District Ganganagar for the offences punishable under Sections 457 and 307 of I.P.C. and under Sections 3(2) (V), 3(2) (VA) of SC/ST Act.

[2024:RJ-JD:8340] (2 of 6) [CRLAS-1854/2023] Learned counsel for the appellant submits that his first criminal appeal against rejection of appeal order passed by learned trial court was dismissed with the liberty to file afresh after recording the statement of Mrs.
Sarabjeet Kaur.

He further submits that examination-in-chief of PW-1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur was recorded by learned trial court on 14.07.2023 and matter was deferred on the request of learned Anil Kumar @ Mannu vs State Of Rajasthan (2024

Public Prosecutor.
Thereafter, injured Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur was again examined on 18.07.2023.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that statement of PW-1 could not be recorded as learned trial court recorded that witnesses is not responding to the answers put by the defence counsel.
The learned trial court with the consent of both the parties deferred the evidence of PW-1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur.

He further submits that thereafter, the next date of hearing was fixed on 20.07.2023 and again an application was filed on behalf of PW-1 indicting the fact that witness is hospitalized and unable to come in the Court for deposing statement.

Again on the request of learned counsel for the complainant, the matter was deferred for recording the statement of PW-1 on 02.08.2023, on that day also PW-1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur did not mark her presence and thereafter bailable warrant was issued by the learned trial court and next date of hearing was fixed on 11.08.2023.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that on 11.08.2023, an application on behalf of the complainant was submitted for adjourning the matter with the contention that an application has been submitted before the Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court indicating the fact that injured Mrs.
Sarabjeet Kaur is not in condition to depose her statement.

That application was opposed [2024:RJ-JD:8340] (3 of 6) [CRLAS-1854/2023] by learned counsel appointed for appellant and learned trial court again reiterated the direction to produce the witness before the Court or to submit the appropriate order passed by the Hon'ble Rajasthan High Court on the application of injured Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur.

He also submits that on the next date of hearing i.e. 19.08.2023, again an application was filed on behalf of the complainant indicating the fact that she has fallen from bed and sustained injuries, therefore, time may be granted for recording her statement.
The learned trial court again fixed date of hearing on 28.08.2023.
Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that afterwards, the trial of the case was stayed on the application filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. by PW-1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur.
The appellant is in custody since 13.07.2022 and in view of stay order, trial cannot be proceeded further.

He also submits that in the statement recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., injured Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur has stated that appellant hit at her head with sharp object, whereas, in statement recorded in the Court as PW-1, she has stated that appellant hit at her head with the aid of sword and thereafter, tried to strangulate her.

Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the complainant party has obtained the stay under Section 482 Cr.P.C., just to deny the bail to the present appellant, therefore, the bail application of appellant may be allowed.

Learned Public Prosecutor as well as the learned counsel appearing on behalf of complainant vehemently oppose the bail application.
[2024:RJ-JD:8340] (4 of 6)
] Learned counsel for the respondents submits that PW-1 is not in position to depose her statement because of her serious ailment.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondents further submit that the first bail application of appellant was dismissed with the liberty after recording statement of injured Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur.

The statement of Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur has yet not been recorded as as she is suffering from serious ailment,
therefore, the bail application of appellant is not maintainable on merits.

Learned counsel for the respondents further submits that due to assault, injured PW-1 suffered grievous injury at her head and injury No.2 at right frontal parietal temporal region was opined to be grievous in nature.

The X-ray report further shows that injured Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur suffered fracture of right frontal parietal and temporal bone involving right frontal sinus and also multiple acute intra cerebral concussion at right parietal temporal region.

After perusing the entire record,
the concerned Medical Jurist has opined the injuries sustained to injured are dangerous to life.

Learned counsel for the respondents further submit that appellant is having criminal antecedents and cases under Sections 363, 366 and 376(1) of I.P.C. and under Section 8/21, 15 of N.D.P.S. Act were instituted against him in 2016 and 2018 respectively, therefore, considering the gravity of the offence, the bail application of appellant may be dismissed.
Heard and perused the record annexed with the bail application.

Vide order dated 20.04.2023, learned counsel for the appellant withdrew the criminal appeal seeking liberty for filing the [2024:RJ-JD:8340] (5 of 6) [CRLAS-1854/2023] criminal appeal afresh after recording of the statement of injured Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur.

This Court dismissed the criminal appeal of the appellant with the liberty to file afresh after recording of the statement of injured Mrs.
Sarabjeet Kaur and also directed the learned trial court to record her statement on priority basis.
The order-sheets of the learned trial court shows that statement of PW- 1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur was recorded on 14.07.2023 and matter was deferred for 18.07.2023.

The order-sheets also shows that cross- examination of injured PW-1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur could not be commenced as she submitted the application for adjourning the matter on the grounds of her ailment.
The stay order dated 06.09.2023 passed in S.B. Criminal Misc. Petition No.5006/2023 is still in operation and vide stay order, the entire trial of the case has been stayed.

Considering the fact that statements of PW-1 Mrs. Sarabjeet Kaur could not be completed and stay order is still operative till 04.03.2024, without commenting anything on the merits of the case and taking into consideration that appellant is in custody since 13.07.2022, so also, the trial of the case may take considerable time, I deem it just and proper to allow the appeal filed by the accused appellant under Section 14-A(1) of SC/ST Act.
Accordingly, this criminal appeal filed under Section 14-A(1) of SC/ST Act is allowed and the order dated 16.08.2023 passed by the learned Special Judge, SC/ST (POA) Act Cases, Sriganganagar in Criminal Misc. Case No.301/2023 is set aside.
